prompt: Some people believe that voting in national elections should be compulsory for all adult citizens. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Compulsory voting is usually argued about as though the disagreement were between people who value participation and people who value liberty. It is not. Almost everyone involved wants a legitimate government chosen by a representative electorate; what they disagree about is whether a law can produce one.

The case for compulsion is stronger than its opponents tend to concede. Voluntary turnout is not random. It correlates closely with age, income and education, so a voluntary electorate is a systematically distorted sample of the population, and parties respond rationally by writing manifestos for the people who show up. Pensioners are courted and renters are not, and the asymmetry compounds over decades into a settlement nobody ever voted for as such. Compulsion corrects the sample, and no amount of enthusiasm for liberty makes that correction unnecessary.

What it cannot correct is the reason people stay away. Non-voting in mature democracies is concentrated among citizens who have concluded, often accurately, that their vote will not change anything where they live. Requiring them to attend converts a withdrawal of consent into a mark on a ballot paper, and the government that results can claim a mandate it has not earned. That is not a minor cost. It removes the only signal the disaffected currently possess, and it removes it precisely when it has become loudest.

There is a version of the policy I would accept. If the legal duty is to attend rather than to endorse, and the ballot carries a formal option to support none of the candidates, the compulsion falls on the state to present itself to every citizen instead of on the citizen to approve of what is presented. Turnout figures then become informative rather than decorative, and abstention survives as something countable.

So I disagree with compulsory voting as it is normally proposed, and would support it in that amended form. Making people vote is, in the end, a way of not asking why they stopped.
title: Compulsory voting
